before: A reference variable can hold null instead of pointing to an object. null is different from an empty String, which is a real object containing no characters.
Calling text.length() when text is null throws NullPointerException. Test text != null before the method call when absence is possible.
text != null && text.length() > 0 asks whether present text is nonempty, without calling length on null.
This example prints false for both null and empty text, but for different reasons: absence skips the method call, while empty text has length zero.
Expected output or behavior: false. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Trace null, empty text, and "Sky". Say whether the length call runs in each case. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: null means a reference points to no object. An empty String is different: it is a real String with no text inside.
Calling length on null throws NullPointerException, an error caused by trying to use a missing object. Check for null before calling a method when the object may be missing.
text != null checks that an object is present. With &&, Java runs the length check only when that first check is true.
The combined check asks whether text exists and has some content. Missing text fails the first check. Empty text passes the first check but fails the length check.
The program prints false. text is null, so Java skips length instead of trying to call it on a missing object.
The quiz replaces null with an empty String. Decide whether length now runs, then decide whether its answer is greater than zero.

before.question: Change text to the empty String "". What happens?
choices: The code throws because empty text is null.
It prints false after safely checking a real object’s zero length.
It prints true because every String is nonempty.
before.explanation: The reference is present, so length runs and returns zero.

after.question: Change text to the empty String "". What happens?
choices: It throws an error because empty text is null.
It prints false after length returns zero.
It prints true because every String contains text.
after.explanation: An empty String is present, so length runs. Its length is zero, which is not greater than zero.
